_comment: Performance-review backlog — the parking lot for STRATEGY TRADING follow-ups: tweak ideas to revisit when more data lands, performance puzzles that need a second window, low-grade clusters worth investigating, comparisons to backtests/sweeps that prior sessions noticed but did not have enough evidence to propose as a Tier-3 change yet. items.title: The M31 P5 candidate lever cannot be backtested — rr_from_here does not exist in the harness
items.source: docs/design/m31-p5-telemetry-reading-lever-PROPOSAL.md section 5, precondition 3
items.detail: P5 precondition 3 reads 'a walk-forward on the rr_from_here floor CLEARS the do-nothing arm'. That is not runnable today: scripts/backtest_trend.py implements stale_exit_bars, giveback_min_mfe_r/giveback_r and trail_decay_* (verified as a POSITIVE CONTROL -- the same probe finds all three at scripts/backtest_trend.py:221-229 and :1038-1046) and finds NOTHING for rr_from_here / r_to_target / r_to_stop / rr_floor. The quantity exists in exactly one module repo-wide: src/runtime/position_telemetry.py, which is LIVE and observe-only. So the harness cannot express the lever whose backtest evidence the precondition asks for.
items.why_it_matters: M31's whole premise is that a lever must be checkable, and P5's gate is 'the same backtest gate as every other lever'. A precondition phrased as 'run the walk-forward' over a lever the harness cannot express is the same shape as the defects this milestone exists to close -- a claim about backtest evidence that no artifact could ever have produced. Sequencing consequence: precondition 3 was described in the S-M31-TERMINAL-STAMP sprint log and the P5 proposal as 'the only remaining item that is runnable work rather than waiting'. That is still true in kind but understates the size: it is IMPLEMENT-then-measure, not measure.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) implement an rr_from_here floor in scripts/backtest_trend.py's monitor path and re-word precondition 3 as the two steps it actually is, or (b) if the lever turns out not to be expressible in the harness's bar model, say so explicitly in the proposal and retire the candidate rather than leaving a precondition that cannot be satisfied. Tractability note, so the next session does not re-derive it: the inputs ARE present -- the harness already carries tp_cap_pct/tp_r (a target) and the stop geometry (atr_stop_mult), which is what r_to_target/r_to_stop need.
items.next_action: Before any P5 walk-forward: add the lever to the harness behind its own flag, and grade it with scripts/research/m20_wf_effective.py so inert folds are excluded from the win count (BL-20260817-FLEET-SWEEP-WF-COUNTS-INERT-FOLDS-AS-WINS -- measured at 75 of 386 ok folds, 19.4%). Tier-1: the harness is not the order path.
items.resolution: Resolution (a): the lever is implemented. scripts/backtest_trend.py gains --rr-floor (default 0.0, byte-identical; registered in ALL_LEVERS_AT_DEFAULT so the per-lever no-op guard covers it). It is NOT a second derivation: src/runtime/position_telemetry.py::r_distances was extracted as the ONE definition of (r_to_stop, r_to_target, rr_from_here), build_record now routes through it, and the harness IMPORTS it -- pinned by object identity plus a source check that the live writer still calls it. Positive control on the bundled fixture: floors 10/25/40/100 fire 1/50/176/315 times, monotone, so the lever is demonstrably not wired to nothing. Precondition 3 is re-worded in the proposal as the two steps it actually is. THE MEASURE HALF IS NOT DONE -- see PB-20260817-RR-FLOOR-UNMEASURED-ON-LIVE-REGIME-DATA.

items.source: Operator question 2026-07-07: 'check if anything trading on alpaca paper can trade on ibkr paper as well.' Finding: NO, as built. IBClient._build_contract (src/units/accounts/ib_client.py) wires ONLY three FUTURES contracts — MES (CME), MGC + MHG (COMEX) — and raises ValueError for any other symbol; there is ZERO equity/ETF (STK) support anywhere in the IB path (no secType='STK', no Stock() construction). alpaca_paper trades equity ETFs (SPY/QQQ/GLD/IWM/TLT/IEF/SLV/USO/GDX/TQQQ/QLD). So none of the alpaca ETF strategies can run on ib_paper without first building STK support. Operator answer 2026-07-07: 'Yes — scope the build.'
items.title: Scope + build IBKR equity/ETF (STK) contract support so the alpaca ETF strategies can also run on ib_paper (2nd paper venue / future IBKR ETF real-money route)
items.description: APPROVED TO SCOPE (operator 2026-07-07). IBKR can trade all the alpaca ETFs (SPY/QQQ/GLD/etc.) as US equities, but the IB integration only knows the 3 micro-futures. To let the ETF strategies mirror onto ib_paper (a second paper venue, cross-broker validation, and a path to an eventual IBKR real-money ETF route) the build needs: (1) IBClient._build_contract: add an STK branch (ib_insync Stock(symbol, 'SMART', 'USD') with primaryExchange hints) alongside the Future branch, gated by a per-symbol instrument-type map (futures MES/MGC/MHG vs equity SPY/QQQ/...); (2) tick sizing / min-tick + contract_value_usd handling for equities (shares, $1 multiplier) vs the futures multipliers already wired in config/instruments.yaml; (3) whole-share qty (equities are whole-unit like Alpaca — reuse the risk.WHOLE_UNIT_QTY_EXCHANGES / requires_whole_unit_qty path, extend to interactive_brokers-equities); (4) market-hours gating (RTH for equities, already handled for the alpaca ETF strategies via 'US market closed' — confirm it applies on the IB path); (5) add the chosen ETF symbols to ib_paper.symbols + route the strategies in accounts.yaml (Tier-3); (6) the mandatory account_compat_matrix run for ib_paper before any real-money IBKR ETF wire. NON-TRIVIAL — this is a new instrument class on an existing broker (new-broker-skill-adjacent), not a routing toggle. NO URGENT GAP: the ETFs already soak on alpaca_paper, so this is for redundancy / a future IBKR ETF real-money option. NEXT STEP: write the design doc (docs/integrations/ibkr-equity-etf-support-DESIGN.md) enumerating the contract map + sizing + hours + the per-symbol instrument-type resolver, for operator review before implementation.

items.title: htf_pullback_trend_2h paper metrics heavily contaminated by June-7 mass reconciliation artifacts — do not judge this strategy on bybit_1 paper PnL
items.description:
The bybit_1 (paper) htf_pullback_trend_2h reported stats (-$11,987, 16.7% WR, 36 trades) are NOT a reliable signal of the strategy's edge. Root cause: on June 7 2026 a mass reconciliation sweep closed ALL open htf paper positions simultaneously at the same exit price. Two clusters: (1) 8 concurrent BTCUSDT SHORT positions (opened 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07, entries 60,579–61,931) all swept by reconciler_filled at exactly 66,356.3 — BTC had run +8% against each short entry, so each trade booked ~-$935 to -$1,818, contributing ~-$9,949 of the overall loss. (2) 4 concurrent LONG positions (opened 2026-06-04/05, entries ~62,050–63,122) all swept at 63,122.9 simultaneously. These 12 concurrent positions existed because the per-strategy netting guard was NOT unconditional for paper accounts before 2026-06-17 — it became unconditional baseline on that date (POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ENABLED removal, BL-20260615-MGCNAKED). The guard now prevents concurrent same-strategy positions; this class of error cannot recur.

Live track record (bybit_2): 6 trade rows, of which ~3 are dust-qty reconciler artifacts (qty=4e-06). The 3 real trades: 67% WR, +$15.47 — too few to be meaningful. Additionally, 15 of 18 signal events on bybit_2 were rejected sized_qty=0 (1.5% risk at bybit_2's small real balance doesn't reach the minimum BTC contract size at current prices). This suppression will naturally relieve as bybit_2's balance grows from other strategy profits (eth/xrp/ada).

Decision (2026-06-30): leave htf_pullback_trend_2h on bybit_2 unchanged — it is harmless, correctly wired, and positioned to accumulate a real track record as the balance grows. Do NOT use bybit_1 paper PnL to make any Tier-3 decision about this strategy.

items.result_2026_08_12:
RESULT 2026-08-12T01:25Z — PARTIAL, and the partition is the point. STEP (2) IS ANSWERED FOR THE 1h SIBLING AND UNANSWERABLE FOR THE PRIMARY 1d LEG ON THIS SPLIT. Reporting them together as one 'TLT result' would be the population error this repo keeps paying for.

tlt_pullback_1h — the floor HURTS. Control 468 IS / 56 OOS at net_R +20.8991 / -5.4769; at floor 0.10 463 / 55 at +12.3272 / -5.3543. So it removes FIVE in-sample trades and costs -8.57R, about 1.7R per trade discarded, while OOS moves +0.12 (noise on n=55). The 0.10 optimum does not reproduce here.

tlt_pullback_1d — UNGRADEABLE, not negative. Base OOS n is **4** on the 2025-07-01 split (control and arm alike), so all 14 cells returned `insufficient_base` under MIN_OOS_TRADES=25. Four daily trades cannot distinguish a real effect from noise, and the floor refusing them is the gate working, not a finding. The primary leg this row is ABOUT therefore has no answer from this run; it needs an earlier split or more history, and a daily leg may simply not have enough post-2025-07 data to be gradeable on the M20 split at all.

CROSS-FAMILY PATTERN, the genuinely new thing. The same axis was measured on ict_scalp the same night (SRQ-20260618-003) and also came back anti-predictive: floors removed trades worth ~+0.58R to +0.75R apiece and made every leg worse. That is now TWO families with TWO unrelated confidence formulas — ict_scalp's 0.4*body_to_range + 0.3*sweep_depth + 0.3*fvg_size blend, and the pullback harness's own score — both of which shed disproportionately PROFITABLE trades when floored. Neither result transfers to the other by construction, which is exactly why two independent negatives are worth more than one: 'a confidence floor improves selection' should no longer be anyone's default prior in this system, and any future proposal for one carries the burden of proof.

items.title: Evaluate whether the daily ETF Donchian trend sleeve should gate on regime/ADX (or a min_confidence floor)
items.description: Design tension, NOT a confirmed bug: classic Donchian trend-following takes the breakout regardless of current ADX (ADX lags; filtering breakouts as 'chop' would miss trend initiations), so min_confidence:0.0 + no regime gate are defensible defaults for a breakout strategy. BUT a low-ADX/chop breakout entry is exactly the kind that can whipsaw, and the sleeve runs unfiltered. Resolve with EVIDENCE before touching config: (1) run the standalone backtest harness on ETF daily history for each sleeve member, comparing baseline vs an ADX/regime filter variant (and a min_confidence sweep) on win rate, expectancy, PnL, hold time, and whipsaw/MFE-MAE; (2) once live closed-trade history accrues, characterize realized performance of low-ADX breakouts vs trend-confirmed ones. The sleeve was added 2026-06-20 (~2 days old at open) so there is effectively no live PnL base yet — any gate now would be unevidenced. Do NOT change config/strategies.yaml min_confidence or add a regime gate without that evidence attached to the Tier-3 PR.
items.trigger_condition: Either a completed backtest of the ADX-regime-filter / min_confidence variants for the daily ETF sleeve, OR enough accrued closed-trade history across the sleeve (e.g. >= 20-30 closed) to compare low-ADX vs trend-confirmed breakout outcomes.
items.resolution_criteria: Either a Tier-3 PR proposing a regime/confidence gate for the named sleeve members citing backtest + live evidence, OR a documented decision (in this item) to keep the unfiltered Donchian breakout with the rationale and the evidence that supports it.

updates.note: RESOLVED — keep the sleeve UNFILTERED (no regime/ADX gate, no min_confidence floor). Evidence: scripts/backtest_trend.py (live-parity trend_donchian; donchian=30, atr_period=14, atr_stop_mult=2.5, trail_mult=4.0, long_only), net-of-fee @ 2bps roundtrip (Alpaca commission-free + tight ETF spread), yfinance daily 2015-01-02..2026-06-18 (~11.5y). Scope = the 3 TREND members (iwm/spy/qqq_trend_long_1d); the 3 pullback members (gld/tlt/ief_pullback_1d) use a different entry with no matching harness and remain unevaluated (see below). Sleeve totals: baseline 93 trades net +63.26R (exp 0.680/trade); adx>=20 77t +48.03R; adx>=25 59t +24.52R; adx>=30 32t +15.79R — an ADX floor MONOTONICALLY REDUCES net profit. Per-symbol baseline expectancy: SPY 1.035, QQQ 1.047 (both clearly HURT by any ADX gate), IWM 0.108 (the weak one; adx>=20 helps IWM specifically 3.90->7.30R but on a small 36->22 trade sample, and adx>=25/30 then hurt it). min_confidence sweep (0..0.16): no consistent gain — per-symbol 'optima' (IWM 0.02, SPY 0.06, QQQ 0.16) are noise-level vs the 0.0 baseline. Conclusion: the current config (min_confidence:0.0, no regime gate) is vindicated; the incident trade (IWM, ADX 11.4) looked bad in isolation but low-ADX breakouts are NOT systematically unprofitable, and filtering them removes the trend-initiation entries that carry the edge. NO config change proposed. Caveats: modest sample (27-36 trades/symbol over 11.5y); yfinance daily approximates but is not identical to the live IBKR feed; the pullback trio is uncovered. Optional future revisit ONLY if warranted by live data: an IWM-only adx>=20 gate is marginally better in-sample but low-N / overfit-risk — not worth a per-symbol special-case now.

PULLBACK TRIO now covered (closes the 'uncovered' caveat above). Evidence: scripts/backtest_pullback.py (live-parity htf_pullback_trend; each member's exact config/strategies.yaml params — GLD tl40/pl15/frac0.618/stop2.0/trail4.0, TLT tl40/pl10/frac0.618/stop2.5/trail5.0, IEF tl30/pl10/frac0.5/stop2.5/trail5.0), net-of-fee @ 2bps, yfinance daily 2015-01-02..2026-06-18. Sleeve totals (GLD+TLT+IEF): baseline 167 trades net +67.32R (exp 0.403/trade); adx>=20 104t +54.61R; adx>=25 70t +19.38R; min_confidence 0.05 166t +67.66R; min_confidence 0.10 163t +71.85R. Per-member baseline net: GLD +37.43 (exp 0.535), TLT +17.60 (0.345), IEF +12.28 (0.267) — all positive. Same shape as the trend trio: an ADX floor REDUCES total net R (67->55->19) though it lifts per-trade expectancy by cutting trades; per-symbol IEF adx>=20 actually improves (12.28->17.93R, exp 0.267->0.578) and GLD adx>=20 lifts expectancy, but TLT adx>=20 hurts (17.60->9.66R) and the sleeve total drops, so no global ADX gate. min_confidence: a ~0.10 floor is a MILD sleeve gain (67.32->71.85R) concentrated almost entirely in TLT (17.60->25.87R at 0.10); GLD/IEF ~flat. FINAL: keep the full 6-symbol daily ETF sleeve UNFILTERED (combined baseline ~+130.6R / 260 trades, 11.5y net-of-fee). One flagged-for-later, evidence-backed but low-priority idea: a TLT-only min_confidence ~0.10 floor (+~8R in-sample, n=49) — revisit with accrued live data before any per-symbol Tier-3 change; not worth acting on blind now. Same caveats as the trend note (modest samples; yfinance~IBKR daily).

ATTEMPTED TWO WAYS, NOT SETTLED — but the attempt narrowed WHERE the answer lives, which is why this is not just a carry-forward.

1. REPO SIDE — checked first, and it cannot answer the question. src/runtime/regime/vol_detector.py holds NO static edge table. It resolves vol_bucket_labels / vol_bucket_edges out of the REGISTRY regime specs at runtime (_SOURCE = 'vol-bucket-edges'), and adopts edges only from a head whose estimator matches rolling_log_return_vol. So the coverage set is a property of the LIVE REGISTRY, not of checked-in code, and no local enumeration is possible. That also means a head can exist for a pair and still contribute no usable edge — a THIRD state the row's binary framing (has-edges / lacks-edges) does not have a slot for, and which must not be folded into 'no head'.

2. /api/bot/ml/registry (diag #8989) — INSUFFICIENT. The page truncated, and within what returned there were 5 distinct model_ids, ZERO occurrences of the key `vol_bucket_edges`, and zero regime heads. I am NOT reading that as 'no head carries edges': the absence is equally explained by the endpoint not exposing model_state at all, which I did not verify. A zero over an unestablished denominator is not a finding.

Severity stays LOW and this is explicitly NOT worth more relay round-trips against the higher-value rows in flight — recording the narrowing so the next session starts from the right surface instead of repeating both dead ends.

items.description: Tested whether the one durable roster winner (trend_donchian) transfers to an uncorrelated market (SPX/MES) for diversification. RESULT: two-sided trend_donchian is net-NEGATIVE on SPX at every tested lookback (dc=20 net -13.5R, dc=30 -14.2, dc=40 -29.1, dc=55 -29.9). BUT the entire loss is the SHORT side; the LONG side is net-POSITIVE at every lookback: long-only net R = +22.45 (dc=20), +16.69 (dc=30), +9.45 (dc=40), +7.20 (dc=55). SPX's secular uptrend systematically punishes trend-breakout shorts (short-side net ~ -31..-38R across configs). Shorter lookback is clearly best (dc=20: 278 long trades, long-side exp ~ +0.08 R/trade, net-positive in 2021/2023/2024; longer lookbacks degrade both sides). maxDD grows with lookback (27.6R @ dc=20 -> 39R @ dc=55). LEAD: a long-only / long-biased trend_donchian on SPX/MES is a plausible diversification add — uncorrelated to the BTC roster, exploits the equity risk premium, positive long-side expectancy. CAVEATS: in-sample over the available 6.4y; SPX500 CFD prices (live is MES — execution/contract differ); long-side R is the long legs of the two-sided run (entries are independent, so it equals a true long-only run, but a dedicated long-only + walk-forward + corr-to-BTC-trend_donchian check should confirm before any proposal). items.description: Phases 1+2 of the regime router are live (PRs #2582, #2583). Phase 2 emits `event=regime_shadow_gate` audit rows with `enforced: false` for every OFF-cell intent the policy table (config/regime_policy.yaml) WOULD suppress; the aggregator's decision is unchanged. Phase 3 is the operator-approved Tier-3 step that turns the OFF cells into hard gates inside aggregate_intents(), behind a single `REGIME_ROUTER_ENABLED` env-var with a one-flag rollback. Pre-conditions before opening the PR: (1) accrue at least a week of live shadow data (~7 days); (2) pull /api/diag/audit filtered to event=regime_shadow_gate, count per (strategy, regime, side); (3) cross-reference with the actual fills + closed PnL of those same intents — confirm the would-gate decisions correlate with the matrix's net-negative cells (vwap OFF everywhere, fvg OFF chop, trend-short OFF trending+transitional, htf_pullback OFF chop). If the live shadow data CONTRADICTS the matrix's verdict for any cell (e.g. vwap actually earned in trending despite the matrix saying -6,179 R), pause and re-investigate before turning the gate on. Implementation: in src/runtime/intents.py::aggregate_intents, drop OFF-cell candidates from `candidates` before the rest of the logic AND emit `event=regime_hard_gate` with `enforced: true`. Hidden behind `os.environ.get('REGIME_ROUTER_ENABLED', '0')` — operator flips the env on the live VM via set-env operator action; rollback is one env flip + restart. items.title: Regime router phase 4 — graduate to soft weights + classifier-v0 detector [Tier-3]
items.description: Phase 4 (the design doc's last step): once phase-3 hard gates have demonstrated lift in production for >= a few weeks, graduate the policy from binary on/off to soft confidence weights (numeric cells like 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 multiply intent.confidence before priority resolution). The phase-2 evaluator already parses `weight: N.N` cells and routes them as permissive with a tagged reason — phase 4 wires the multiplier in. Also: validate `regime-classifier-baseline-v0` (the shadow regime model in the registry) against ADX-14 on the same per-tick stream; if its predictions correlate >0.85 with ADX-14 and add value at the regime boundaries (the 18.5-22.5 ADX hysteresis zone the design doc Q4 flagged), swap the detector source from 'adx-14' to 'classifier-v0' in src/runtime/regime/detector.py (the audit-row `regime_source` field already supports this; consumer is forward-compatible).

items.title: Retire the trend_donchian long_only flag once the regime router policy table subsumes it [Tier-3, follow-up to phase 3]
items.description: trend_donchian's `long_only: true` flag in config/strategies.yaml was shipped as #2570 (2026-06-01) as a simple, robust win that dropped the strategy's -37 R short drag. The regime router's policy table independently mirrors the same constraint: trend_donchian.short is OFF in trending+transitional (the regimes where the -52 R loss concentrates) and ON in chop (the +16 R chop-short edge). Once phase 3 (PERF-20260601-006) is live and the table is enforcing those gates, the strategy-level long_only flag becomes redundant — both flags would be saying the same thing in trending/transitional, AND the table is the ONLY way to recover the chop-short edge. The cleanup is: flip `long_only: false` (or remove the field entirely) on trend_donchian in config/strategies.yaml AND remove the `_short_suppressed_long_only` branch in src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py / strategy_signal_builders.py. The router policy table will then be the single source of truth for trend_donchian's direction gating. Operator's instruction 2026-06-01: "leave that for now" — keep long_only as defense-in-depth until phase 3 proves out the policy-table enforcement. Mechanical risk if NOT cleaned up after phase 3: when an operator-approved exception manually flips a cell in regime_policy.yaml (e.g. enable trend_donchian chop-short in some future regime study), the YAML-level long_only flag will silently override and suppress that intent — a confusing footgun.

items.title: Degenerate signal confidence: vwap + htf_pullback_trend_2h emit confidence=1.0 on EVERY order package — carries no information for gating/sizing/ML
items.description: In the 2026-06-01 window every vwap (17/17) and htf_pullback_trend_2h (2/2) order package carried confidence=1.0 exactly, while trend_donchian emitted a genuine graded value (0.392). A confidence hard-pinned at 1.0 is degenerate: it can't drive a min-confidence floor, can't size by conviction, and feeds the shadow ML models (setup_quality etc.) a constant feature. Likely the signal builders for these two strategies set confidence=1.0 as a placeholder rather than computing it from setup strength (e.g. vwap: distance-in-sigma from the band; htf: pullback depth / trend strength). NOT a live-capital bug today (vwap+htf are execution:shadow) but it (a) blunts any future min-confidence gate, (b) pollutes the ML feature, (c) makes per-decision grading rely on geometry alone. CHECK src/runtime/strategy_signal_builders.py for the vwap + htf confidence assignment.

items.title: Bucket artifact-heavy paper records: gradeable round-trips vs technical artifacts vs broker-truncated-reconstructable
items.description: Per-strategy performance is distorted by paper records that are NOT clean strategy round-trips: intent-layer reduce/flip legs (intent_reduce=true), netting-guard/hold-policy suppressions (reentry_suppressed_*/flip_suppressed_*), reconciler_filled closes with no classifiable bracket reason, and orphan/re-adopt flaps. Proposed taxonomy: (A) GRADEABLE round-trips = open that reached a genuine sl/tp or strategy monitor() exit -> the ONLY rows that drive win-rate/expectancy; (B) TECHNICAL ARTIFACTS (reduce/flip/netting/hold/unclassified-reconciler/orphan-flap/creds-refusal) -> route to the technical/health backlog, exclude from the strategy scorecard; (C) BROKER-TRUNCATED-RECONSTRUCTABLE = trade closed mid-flight by reconciler/stuck-watchdog but we have entry+SL+TP -> keep the decision (entry quality, R:R) and reconstruct the would-be outcome by replaying /api/bot/candles from entry forward (first-touch SL vs TP within the bracket) -> label reconstructed_win/reconstructed_loss/open_at_window_end. Build as a performance-review pre-filter (+ optional reconstruction pass) so aggregates exclude bucket B by construction. Analysis/tooling layer, NOT a live-path change. Recommend operator OK to build it next; affects how every per-strategy number is computed.
items.trigger_condition: Next performance-review run, or when the operator approves building the bucketing pre-filter.
items.resolution_criteria: A performance-review step that classifies each closed paper record into bucket A/B/C, excludes B from per-strategy win-rate/expectancy, and reconstructs C outcomes from candles; documented + applied to one review.

updates.note: BUILT the bucketing tool: src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py (pure A/B/C classifier) + src/analysis/trade_reconstruction.py (pure first-touch SL/TP reconstruction + candle adapter) + scripts/analysis/classify_paper_records.py (CLI, --json/--db, --reconstruct) + tests (21 passing). Validated on the real 2026-06-26 window (issue #4654, 48 recs): 0 gradeable / 46 artifact / 2 reconstructable. Wired into performance-review SKILL.md (run pre-filter before aggregates; compute over bucket-A only + bucket-C reconstructed). Shipped on branch claude/order-packages-zero-qty-eaofnv / PR #4660. REMAINING to close: apply it in one live performance-review run and confirm the per-strategy A/B/C split + reconstructed outcomes land in the report.

RESOLVED this session -- the resolution criteria ('a performance-review step that classifies each closed paper record into bucket A/B/C, excludes B from win-rate/expectancy, and reconstructs C outcomes from candles; documented + applied to one review') is now met. Ran `scripts/analysis/classify_paper_records.py` against this window's 19 real closed trades (all funding classes): 1 gradeable (A, bybit_2 eth_pullback_2h sl exit), 18 artifact (B, mostly closeReason='other'/'reconciler'), 0 reconstructable (C) this pass. In the course of running it for real, found + fixed TWO bugs that were silently defeating the tool when fed its own documented input source (`/api/bot/trades/closed`): (1) the classifier only read DB-native column names, never the API's camelCase shape, so every API-shaped row silently misclassified as 'unclassified' bucket B regardless of the true exit; (2) `_CLEAN_EXIT_REASONS` was missing `exit_head`/`stale_stop` (legitimate M20 strategy-monitor exits). Both fixed + verified against real data this session (commit 081b920), 11/11 existing unit tests still green. The pre-filter step is now genuinely usable end-to-end from a diag-relay pull, which is what this item asked for.

Maker execution CANNOT rescue the stop-based scalps: their exit is inherently a taker event, so maker-entry/taker-exit (realistic bound) stays net-negative; only both-legs-maker clears them, which stop strategies can't do. The one class that CAN be both-legs-maker is the market-neutral FUNDING CARRY (exits on funding-decay/timeout, no price stop). RESOLVED (trainer #6493, neutral carry at TAKER 7.5 vs MAKER 1.0 vs ZERO, 3yr + OOS 2025-01+): maker execution IS the lever — at 1.0bps full-history net recovers ~70% of the gross funding harvest with tiny drawdown: ETH +0.70→+7.72R, SOL +0.98→+6.46R, BNB -1.87→+11.03R (maxDD 0.05–0.68R). BUT the current-regime OOS (2025-01+) maker net is thin-to-negative: ETH +0.40R, SOL +0.07R (flat), BNB -0.61R — the win is front-loaded 2023-24; funding compressed post-2024 (confirms PB-20260620-002). VERDICT: real, regime-gated candidate, NOT live-now. RE-TRIGGER: re-run the neutral-carry OOS maker net when funding elevates; only if a CURRENT-regime OOS maker net clears a meaningful bar (not the front-loaded 3yr average) is a Tier-3 proposal warranted for (a) a post-only/limit carry executor + (b) wiring the neutral-carry sleeve (incl. account_compat_matrix). Do NOT build post-only entry for the stop-based scalps (exits stay taker). Xsec momentum parked (4-symbol universe too small).

items.title: Market-neutral crypto cointegration PAIRS sleeve — the M22 reliable-tool finding (Tier-3, drafted)
items.detail: M22's reliable small-TF tool: market-neutral crypto cointegration pairs at 1h (SOL/BTC, BNB/BTC, ETH/BTC, SOL/ETH). FULLY VALIDATED as research: profitable (3yr +350..+541R), OOS-robust (held-out 2025-26 +158..+177R, NO expectancy decay, 58-60% win, maxDD 6-15R), capital-efficient (~0.8-1.2 net_R/pos-day, OOS 0.93-1.12 — the operator's original PnL-per-time metric, beats scalps+cash), cointegration-STABLE (half-life ~12h, mean-reverting in 100% of 30-day windows over 3yr, no breaks, spread bounded 100%), funding-NEGLIGIBLE (~0.5 bps/trade vs a much larger R-edge), fee-insensitive (spread-stop R dwarfs fees). Sidesteps BOTH small-TF root causes. TIER-3 PROPOSAL DRAFTED (pairs-sleeve-PROPOSAL-2026-07-15.md): the architectural lift is that a pair is a 2-LEG simultaneous-position strategy that does NOT fit the single-symbol intent model -> needs a NEW isolated pairs-executor primitive (place both legs atomically, leg-imbalance guard, spread-exit management) + account_compat_matrix + a phased shadow->demo(bybit_1)->real(bybit_2) rollout. REMAINING before live: (a) $-return-on-2-leg-margin sizing (a proposal/RiskManager choice, not a research number); (b) execution realism (2-leg simultaneous fills + slippage — only a live/paper soak settles it). OPEN OPERATOR DECISIONS: proceed to build the pairs executor + shadow soak (P-A)? which pairs (SOL/BTC+BNB/BTC best, or all 4)? concurrency/sizing caps (pairs share the BTC leg = correlated)? Cheap follow-up: fetch btcusdt_funding.csv to the trainer to confirm the /BTC pairs' funding drag (only SOL/ETH ran; the /BTC pairs are representative-by-analogy). items.title: M27 Batch-2: ict_scalp 5m fires only 8-16 trades/yr on IBKR micro futures — diagnose data-continuity vs genuine rarity before any futures scalp verdict
items.detail: Config-exact ict_scalp_5m on native IBKR 5m over ~1y produced MES 16 / MGC 14 / MHG 8 trades — ~18x fewer than crypto (~285/yr), so the k-fold is 2-4 trades/fold and NO gate verdict is possible (findings: docs/research/M27-P0-batch2-futures-findings-2026-07-21.md). The 5m frozen vol terciles are degenerate (q33=0.0 on all three — overnight flat/identical-close bars); only the 15m label is healthy. Two candidate causes to distinguish before spending more compute: (a) genuine setup rarity in the RTH-gapped futures tape (→ futures scalp belongs at 15m+, P1), or (b) a stitched-ContFuture 5m data-continuity artifact (roll-boundary gaps) suppressing the rolling-window FVG/sweep detector. Repro: /home/ubuntu/m27_out_fut on the trainer; CSVs /home/ubuntu/m27_data/{MES,MGC,MHG}_5m.csv. Prereq before any M27 P1 futures-15m run.
items.resolution_note: 2026-07-21 (diagnostic): diagnostic script (scripts/research/m27/diagnose_futures_gaps.py, PR #7276) run against the real CSVs (trainer relay #7279) resolves (a) vs (b) in favor of (b)-dominant, evidenced not inferred: MES 48.9% / MGC 50.8% / MHG 86.0% of all bars are part of runs of byte-identical consecutive closes, and 61.4% / 72.0% / 96.6% of the strategy's own 20-bar rolling windows contain such a run — the direct mechanism behind the degenerate q33=0.0 vol terciles AND a plausible major suppressor of the FVG/sweep detector. The flat-bar % ranks MES<MGC<MHG, matching real-world liquidity ordering of these micro contracts, consistent with the useRTH=False 24h Globex pull folding in genuinely thin overnight sessions — but not conclusively disambiguated from a pull/pipeline artifact (some long flat runs extend into what should be RTH). Full write-up: docs/research/M27-P0-batch2-futures-gap-diagnostic-2026-07-21.md. 2026-07-21 (repull-followup, RESOLVED): executed the prescribed “go coarser” next step — reused the already-pulled 15m IBKR shards (no new live-VM pull), converted + re-ran config-exact backtest+kfold at 15m. Trade counts roughly doubled (MES 16→31/yr, MGC 14→31/yr) but MHG actually DROPPED (8→5) and none reach statistical significance; MES/MGC kfold baseline is net-negative (1/4 and 2/4 folds respectively), MHG stayed underpowered (5 trades, 2/4 folds empty). This confirms the diagnostic's conclusion — the thin-liquidity characteristic is genuine, not a resolvable data-pull artifact, and coarsening the bars does not manufacture setups that aren't there. Full write-up: docs/research/M27-P0-repull-followups-2026-07-21.md.

*** READ THIS FIRST — 2026-08-08 CORRECTION (session system-review-ma0ava). ***
The headline claim below is substantially WRONG and must not drive a Tier-2 order-monitor/bracket fix as written.

POPULATION: the 3 AVAXUSDT/bybit_1 trades whose fills fall in the 7-day window — 4314, 4361, 4413. The window holds EXACTLY 6 AVAX fills (3 entries + 3 exits), first_exec_time 18:33:23.795Z matches 4314's created_at to the second, and open_qty_signed is 0. The population is closed.
  journal sum of the 3 rows      -$9,669.41
  exchange FIFO, net of $233.91  -$5,403.09
  journal OVERSTATES by          -$4,266.32  (79%)

MECHANISM, confirmed in the timestamps: the last real AVAX fill is 10:00:58.915Z, but the journal closed 4361 at 10:17:15.670 and 4413 at 10:17:17.008 — ~16 minutes AFTER the position was already flat — and stamped BOTH with the same bar close 6.416 despite different entries (6.788 / 6.692) and different stops (6.46475 / 6.6592). That is a detection-time bar anchor, not a fill. So 4413's -$4,254.24 / -8.41R is substantially a reconstruction artifact, and the 'the stop let price run 8x past it' reading is not supported.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not asserted: the per-trade split of the $4,266 across 4314/4361/4413. No corrected R is claimed for 4413 specifically. Also unknown whether 4413 was among the 39 rows repaired to MEASURED by the 2026-08-08 backfill-fabricated-exits apply (issue #8628) or among the 28 left as fills_present_but_qty_unreconciled — netted siblings sharing one exchange position are exactly the shape that lands in the latter. CHECK: read trade 4413's notes.backfill and exit_price_source before quoting any R for it.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, and is still worth working:
  * the ~16-minute detection lag is real and independently confirmed;
  * 7 of 10 closes by reconciler rather than by stop or target is a per-CLOSE-PATH count, unaffected by exit-price provenance, and remains the strongest signal here;
  * the hold-time distribution (0.8h..15.8h on a 5m strategy) is timestamp-derived and also unaffected.
  * the giveback figure (mean 1.92R) is NOT safe — it is computed from realized R, which is exactly the quantity shown to be manufactured. Re-derive it over MEASURED-provenance rows only before quoting it again.

The qty-scoped-stop-desync hypothesis below is now COMPETING with a simpler measured explanation rather than being the leading one. It is not disproven — the netting divergence is separately real (BL-20260801) — but this trade is no longer evidence for it.

--- ORIGINAL ROW AS FILED 2026-08-07, retained as the record ---

Trade 4413, ict_scalp_avax_5m, AVAXUSDT long, bybit_1 (PAPER — no money at risk, which is the only reason this is not a P0).
  opened 2026-08-05T08:03:54Z, entry 6.692, sl 6.6592 (a 0.53% / ~1R stop), tp 6.7487
  closed 2026-08-06T10:17:17Z — hold 15.8h on a FIVE-MINUTE strategy
  realized -$4,254.24 = -8.41R. MFE +0.73R, MAE -5.0R.
  closeReason 'reconciler' / exit_reason 'reconciler_filled' — NOT sl_cross.
  Graded B (entry=optimal, conf 0.83): the DECISION was fine. The execution gave away 8.4x the intended risk.

The stop did not contain the loss and did not close the trade; the reconciler noticed the position was gone. Realized -8.41R is also worse than the measured MAE of -5.0R, which implies the fill landed beyond anything the candle window saw.

items.title: [research] The M20 exit-lever gate has NO minimum trade count, and 82% of the cells it passes sit on an OOS base under 50 trades
items.summary: Path A's beats() predicate (net_R AND maxDD no worse on BOTH windows, then a yearly walk-forward) has no minimum trade count. Measured over the 603 corpus cells with a readable OOS base: 35.8% have an OOS base under 10 trades, 65.2% under 50 (median 34, mean 50.0, max 358). Of the 40 cells the sweep PASSES (Path A or path_b_wf_pass), 33 (82%) sit on an OOS base under 50 trades and 13 sit on fewer than 10. So a cell clears the gate by improving net_R and maxDD over a book that may contain three trades, and can then post a 6/6 walk-forward over folds that are nearly empty.
items.evidence: checked: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (604 rows / 603 cells / 51 legs, committed) via a distribution over base_trades_OOS. Concrete instances from the PASS list: spy_trend_long_1d vt_hot90_t2 passes on an OOS base of 3 trades (d_net_r_OOS +0.7995, d_max_dd_OOS exactly 0.0, walk-forward 6/6); qqq_trend_long_1d vt_hot90_t2 on 4 trades (d_net_r_OOS +0.1015, d_max_dd_OOS 0.0, wf 6/6); scha_trend_long_1d vt_hot90_t2 on 5 trades. A d_max_dd of exactly 0.0 is the tell that the lever never touched the drawdown path. The single PASS in the corpus on a solid denominator is trend_donchian_1h vt_hot90_t2.5 (OOS base 168) and that leg reads enabled: false + execution: shadow, retired and unshippable.
items.why_not_fixed: Setting the floor VALUE is the operator's call, and fitting one from the same corpus it will judge would be the exposure-ceiling mistake (gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN sections 6-7: a ceiling with no distribution behind it silently throttles correct work). The exit-refinement SKILL already prescribes the procedure for an unset threshold: the sweep REPORTS the distribution, the operator sets the value. This item reports it.
items.caveat: Unlike the Path B RATE floor answered the same day (`do not set one` -- a rate floor is a PREDICTION claim and both candidate predictors returned no_separation over 604 rows), a minimum trade count is a DENOMINATOR REQUIREMENT, not a fitted threshold, and needs no separation test. The repo already ships this exact shape as research_results_gate.min_trades. Do not conflate the two: one says do not fit a threshold, the other says a missing denominator floor is letting 3-trade books pass.
items.suggested_action: Operator sets a min-OOS-trades floor on the M20 gate (and ideally min-IS too). What the distribution says: a floor of 50 retains 7 of the 40 current passes; a floor of 10 retains 27 of 40. Then re-grade the corpus and re-read docs/research/M20-path-b-floor-and-trail-widen-2026-08-10.md section 5, whose PASS list is currently not floored. Blocks PB-20260811-M20-REGIME-CONDITIONED-EXITS-UNPROVEN, because the floor decides whether those passes are real.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The operator set the floor and it is enforced in code: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:548 defines MIN_OOS_TRADES = 25 with the full cost-curve rationale at :2040-2075 (floor 10 keeps 34 legs/27 passes, 25 keeps 32/27, 50 keeps 20/7 — 25 is the last point before coverage is paid for), and scripts/research/m20_corpus_extract.py:115 records it as 'operator decision 2026-08-11, value 25'. The corpus was then re-graded: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl now holds 660 rows carrying min_oos_trades_floor: 25 across sweeps dated 2026-08-11 through 2026-08-15, with insufficient_base as its own verdict on 160 of them (never folded into is_oos_fail). — Closed on positive evidence — the row's suggested_action (operator sets a min-OOS-trades floor, then re-grade the corpus) is done end-to-end, and the implementation preserves the distinction the row cared about ('we did not look at enough trades' vs 'the lever failed'). The honest limit the enforcement site itself records — that a trade-count floor is a proxy for how many trades the LEVER actually fired on, which the corpus does not record — is a genuine residual and should be filed as its own row if it is to be tracked.

items.title: [research] Regime-conditioned exit selection passes 8/123 vs 13/480 (6.5% vs 2.7%), Fisher p=0.052 -- suggestive, not established
items.summary: vol_trail (vt_hot90 / vt_hot80 / vt_cold10) already IS regime-conditioned exit selection: it keys the trail multiple on a causal ATR percentile rank over a 200-bar window (scripts/backtest_pullback.py:263). Across 41 legs / 123 cells it passes Path A at 6.5% (8/123) vs 2.7% (13/480) for all other exit cells; including path_b_wf_pass, 10.6% vs 5.6%. Fisher exact two-sided p=0.052 (Path A) / 0.065 (either path), BEFORE any correction for the comparison having been chosen after seeing the data. A ~2.4x pass-rate ratio is a lead worth a purpose-built test; it is not a result.
items.evidence: checked: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, partitioning cells on lever == vol_trail (or a vt_ prefixed cell name) and running a stdlib Fisher exact via math.comb. Also checked: an artifact hypothesis of mine was REFUTED. I expected conditioning to thin the population each cell acts on, inflating spurious passes; it does not. Thin OOS bases are fleet-wide, not specific to conditioned cells: median OOS base 32 (vt_*) vs 34 (everything else), 68.3% vs 64.4% under 50 trades; among PASSING cells 29 vs 32 median. So thinness does not explain the gap; it is PB-20260811-M20-GATE-NO-MIN-TRADES-82PCT-THIN, which applies to both arms equally.
items.why_not_fixed: Not supported at this n, so there is nothing to build yet. 12 of the 13 vt_* passes sit on an OOS base under 50 trades, so the min-trades floor decides whether any of them are real. Blocked on that item, not on more sweeping.
items.caveat: Two designs exist and are NOT interchangeable. (A) condition on realized vol -- what vol_trail already does: self-contained, causal, no ML dependency, implementable in the live monitor from candles, and NO axis-fidelity problem because it is not trying to match the router's axis. (B) condition on the router's regime label (ml_vol_regime_for_symbol -> predict_proba(row)[volatile]): matches the ENTRY gate's axis but inherits the advisory head's per-symbol availability (BTC + SOL only) and carries the full regime-selectivity Rule 3 axis-fidelity burden. Recommendation is NEITHER yet: (A) is already measured and does not clear a significance bar, and (B) would add an ML dependency to the exit path to chase an effect (A) has not established.
items.suggested_action: Park until the min-trades floor is set. If the floor leaves a defensible vt_* population, run a purpose-built test (a pre-registered comparison, not a post-hoc partition of a sweep run for another question) before any Tier-3 exit-conditioning proposal.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: MEASURED THIS RUN on the floored corpus, which is exactly the evidence the row said would decide it. Over the 660 rows in docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl carrying min_oos_trades_floor: 25 (sweeps 2026-08-11..08-15), vol_trail/vt_* cells pass Path A at 4/155 = 2.58% vs 14/505 = 2.77% for all other cells (Fisher exact two-sided p = 1.0), and either-path at 10/155 = 6.45% vs 33/505 = 6.53% (p = 1.0). The ~2.4x pass-rate ratio that motivated the row does not survive the min-trades floor it was explicitly blocked on. — Closed as REFUTED at the floor, with the bound stated: the 660 floored rows are newer sweep runs, not a re-grade of the identical 604-row unfloored population, so this rules out the lead at the floor rather than re-scoring the original partition trade-for-trade. That is enough — the row's own recommendation was already NEITHER design, and there is now no separation left to build a purpose-built test around. Reopen only if a pre-registered comparison (not a post-hoc partition) is run and finds otherwise.

items.title: [strategy] ict_scalp_5m is the fleet's most negative base book AND the only negative-on-both-windows leg routed to real money
items.summary: The M20 exit-lever sweep measures each leg's config-exact BASE book before any cell is applied. Over the 51-leg corpus, 4 of the 50 legs with a readable base are negative on BOTH the IS and OOS windows. Exactly one of those four is enabled, execution: live, AND routed to a real_money account -- ict_scalp_5m on bybit_2 -- and it is the most negative of the four by a wide margin: IS -48.88R, OOS -13.31R.
items.evidence: checked: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (604 rows / 603 cells / 51 legs, live-parity geometry, IS/OOS split 2025-07-01, committed f4225f7) for the base books, and config/accounts.yaml + config/strategies.yaml for routing. The four negative-on-both legs: ict_scalp_5m (IS -48.88 / OOS -13.31, enabled, live, REAL MONEY bybit_2); ict_scalp_avax_5m (-37.98 / -23.17, paper only); trend_donchian_1h (-34.19 / -21.21, enabled: false + shadow, inert); fvg_range_15m (-1.88 / -4.68, routed to bybit_2 but execution: shadow, so it places no live order). Denominator for context: 32 of 50 legs are positive on both windows, 14 negative on one.
items.why_not_fixed: Out of tier and out of scope for the session that found it. Whether a strategy trades at all is Tier-3, and this is a STRATEGY-PERFORMANCE question, not the exit-lever question the sweep was run to answer -- no exit lever fixes a base book that loses on both windows, and the sweep confirmed that directly: all 4 ict_scalp_5m cells are honest negatives, and the one cell that cleared IS/OOS on both axes (gb1R_afterMFE1R) then FAILED its walk-forward.
items.caveat: This is the config-exact BACKTEST base, not live realized PnL, and the two must not be conflated -- the live journal's ict_scalp rows also carry a known fabricated-provenance problem (see PB-20260807-ICTSCALP-STOP-DID-NOT-CONTAIN-8R). The claim here is strictly about the backtested base book on the live-parity geometry.
items.suggested_action: A /performance-review pass should compare this backtested base against the leg's MEASURED-provenance live PnL (/api/bot/performance totalPnlMeasured + pnlCoverage per strategy). If live agrees with the backtest, the Tier-3 question is whether ict_scalp_5m should keep its real-money routing on bybit_2 -- demote to bybit_1 paper, or set execution: shadow, both of which are one-line declares. If live disagrees, that disagreement is itself the finding.
items.resolution: REFUTED, with a mechanism. The comparison was run the same day (2026-08-11) and it INVERTS the concern rather than merely failing to confirm it. Live real-money record over window=all: 16 trades, 75.0% win rate, totalPnl +$13.53, totalPnlMeasured +$13.53, pnlCoverage 1.00 (16 of 16 rows MEASURED -- zero fabricated, zero unverified), totalR +46.80. It is the BEST real-money leg in the book by PnL (first of 12 in the descending perStrategy list); the 30d window agrees in sign (4 trades, +$3.17, coverage 1.00). The PB-20260807 fabricated-provenance caveat carried on this item does NOT apply to this population -- coverage is perfect. MECHANISM (this is not 'n=16 got lucky'): config/regime_policy.yaml authors TWO fully-off trend_vol cells for this exact leg -- trending/volatile and chop/volatile, both long:false + short:false -- so live it is refused outright in volatile regimes; it trades BTCUSDT, the one symbol where that gate bites (advisory ML vol head resolves the label, trend_vol cells authored, real-money enforce live since 2026-06-28); and the sweep measured it with the gate OFF, because m20_fleet_exit_sweep passes no --regime-router so backtest_system defaults to 'off' and sets REGIME_ROUTER_DISABLED=1. So -48.88R is the UNGATED book, including exactly the volatile-regime trades production refuses, and +46.80R is the gated book the leg actually trades. The gate was authored to remove that losing regime; the live record is what that looks like working. WHAT WAS WRONG WITH THIS ITEM: not the arithmetic (the base figures are correct for what they measured) but the POPULATION -- it compared a live routing decision against a book that routing does not produce. NO TIER-3 ACTION IS WARRANTED; neither remedy should be applied and the leg keeps its real-money routing on this evidence. RESIDUAL, stated honestly: 16 trades is a thin sample, so this refutes the concern rather than establishing the leg as good -- keep it in the /performance-review watch cadence, not as a P1. The general defect (no corpus row recorded which regime book its base was measured on; 6 of 51 legs / 56 of 604 rows affected) is fixed in the same session and written up in docs/research/M20-path-b-floor-and-trail-widen-2026-08-10.md section 4c; the section-1 'do not set a floor' verdict was re-measured with the policy-named legs excluded (52->45 cells, 22->20 legs) and both predictors stay at no_separation.

items.title: [strategy] tlt_pullback_1h ships trail3 while trail4 passes the walk-forward at LIVE-PARITY geometry, reproduced across three independent runs
items.summary: tlt_pullback_1h has trail_mult 3 shipped (matrix trail_geometry cell = `shipped`, ref: fleet sweep 2026-07-12, Tier-3 PR #6229). The committed sweep corpus contains a `trail4` cell for the same leg graded at LIVE-PARITY take-profit geometry (tp_cap_pct 0.099) that comes back `path_b_wf_pass` -- and it does so in THREE independent runs (2026-08-10T22:42Z, 2026-08-12T00:55Z, 2026-08-13T01:36Z), so it is not a single-run artifact. Nothing in the matrix cell mentions it.
items.evidence: checked: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, the 2026-08-13T01:36:06Z row for leg=tlt_pullback_1h cell=trail4 lever=trail_geometry -- tp_cap_pct 0.099, split 2025-07-01, base_trades_IS 468 / base_trades_OOS 56, d_net_r_IS +35.47 / d_net_r_OOS +5.42, d_max_dd_IS -0.69 / d_max_dd_OOS +1.23, wf_ran true, wf 5/6 usable folds won, path_b_candidate true, path_b_rate_ok true. The base book that delta is measured against ALREADY INCLUDES the shipped trail3, so +5.42 OOS net R is the improvement over what is live today, which is the right comparison. base_trades_OOS 56 independently matches a fresh config-exact measurement of the same leg (trainer relay #9211), so the window is real.
items.caveats: STATED BECAUSE THEY BOUND THE CLAIM. (1) It is a PATH B pass, the weaker route -- gate_passed_OOS is false and it qualified via the Path B rate check; it is not a Path A clean pass. (2) OOS n=56 is comfortably above the floor of 25 but is not large. (3) The three runs share a corpus and a split date, so they are re-measurements of the same window, NOT three independent samples of the world -- they rule out a flaky run, not overfit to that window. (4) I did NOT re-run anything here; this is a read of committed corpus rows. (5) One-lever-per-leg is the standing convention, and trail_geometry is that leg's occupied slot, so this is a CHANGE to the shipped value, not an addition.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the operator approves a Tier-3 trail_mult 3 -> 4 change for tlt_pullback_1h, it merges, and the matrix trail_geometry cell records the live-parity evidence and the new shipped value; or (b) a walk-forward on a window that does NOT share the 2025-07-01 split (or a fresh out-of-window fold) fails to reproduce the edge and the row is closed `resolved_refuted` with those numbers stated; or (c) the operator decides the Path B route is too weak a basis for a real-money parameter change and says so, which closes it as a recorded decision rather than an open question.
items.source: M20 overnight session 2026-08-13 -- found while checking whether the stale trail_geometry decisions could be re-swept

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Confirmed and STRENGTHENED this run. config/strategies.yaml:1986 still ships tlt_pullback_1h trail_mult: 3.0. In docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl the leg=tlt_pullback_1h cell=trail4 row now comes back path_b_wf_pass in FIVE runs (2026-08-10, 08-12, 08-13, 08-14, 08-15) at live-parity geometry tp_cap_pct 0.099, wf 5/6 usable folds won every time, d_net_r_OOS +4.12 to +5.82 — and the last four rows carry min_oos_trades_floor: 25, so it clears the trade-count floor set on 2026-08-11 (OOS base 30-56 vs floor 25) rather than predating it. — TIER-3 PROPOSAL: change config/strategies.yaml::tlt_pullback_1h trail_mult from 3.0 to 4.0 (a strategy parameter, so proposal only) and record the live-parity evidence plus the new shipped value in the exit-refinement coverage matrix trail_geometry cell. Bounds the operator should weigh, stated because they limit the claim: it is a PATH B pass (gate_passed_OOS false, qualified via the rate check), OOS n is 30-56 (above the floor, not large), the five runs share a corpus and the 2025-07-01 split so they rule out a flaky run rather than window overfit, and trail_geometry is this leg's one occupied lever slot so this REPLACES the shipped value. The row's own option (c) — operator judges Path B too weak a basis — is an equally valid close.

2026-08-16 (/system-review sysrev-0816, operator instruction 're-measure before deciding'): THE RE-MEASUREMENT ALREADY EXISTS AND THERE IS NO UN-RUN FRESHER WINDOW. This row's own criterion (b) -- 'a walk-forward on a window that does NOT share the 2025-07-01 split fails to reproduce the edge' -- has now been TESTED TWICE AND DID NOT FAIL: the committed corpus holds FIVE live-parity (tp_cap_pct 0.099) trail4 rows for this leg across THREE distinct splits -- 2025-07-01 (x3, base_OOS 55/56/56), 2025-10-15 (base_OOS 43) and 2025-12-10 (base_OOS 30) -- and trail4 is path_b_wf_pass in ALL FIVE. So caveat (3) (shared split) is closed, and criterion (b) is refuted rather than met. The sibling trail2 is is_oos_fail in four of the five and path_b_wf_fail in the fifth, so the result is trail4-specific, not 'wider trail wins'. WHY THIS STILL DOES NOT SHIP, and it is not the shared-split caveat: TWO disqualifiers reproduce in ALL FIVE runs. (i) gate_passed_OOS is FALSE in every run with gate_reason_OOS `maxdd_worse` -- d_max_dd_OOS +1.227, +1.227, +1.227, +0.800, +0.531, i.e. out-of-sample drawdown is WORSE at trail4 on every window tested (it shrinks as the split moves later but never crosses to <=0). (ii) THE BASE OOS BOOK IS UNPROFITABLE IN EVERY RUN -- base_net_r_OOS -5.477, -5.354, -5.477, -5.451, -2.889 -- against a solidly profitable base IS (+20.899, +12.327, +20.899, +19.509, +20.545). That IS/OOS sign break belongs to the LEG, not the lever, so d_net_r_OOS +4.12..+5.82 is an improvement to a LOSING book on every window -- the same pattern the matrix already cites as discounting the regime_flip PASS. NO FURTHER SPLIT IS AVAILABLE: lifetime is ~518-525 trades, the freshest split already run (2025-12-10) yields base_OOS 30, and MIN_OOS_TRADES is 25 -- so moving the split later than 2025-12-10 drops OOS below the floor. Re-running returns a sixth path_b_wf_pass over a sixth losing base book. THE MATRIX HOLD STANDS AND THIS ROW WAS STALE AGAINST IT: the coverage-matrix trail_geometry cell was set passed_unshipped and deliberately HELD on 2026-08-14 under operator decision (f) with the revisit condition written in -- 'Revisit if the leg's base book turns profitable' -- which this row (opened 2026-08-14T09:48Z, earlier the same day) never picked up. That condition is NOT met on any of the three windows. BLOCKED ON, precisely: base_net_r_OOS > 0 for this leg on a floor-clearing split. Not on another sweep. checked: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (5 trail4 + 5 trail2 rows, leg=tlt_pullback_1h lever=trail_geometry), docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json (tlt_pullback_1h row, trail_geometry cell), config/strategies.yaml (trail_mult: 3.0 live), git log -L on the tlt block.

2026-08-16 PROVENANCE OF THE SHIPPED VALUE, established because a /system-review session nearly reversed it on a bad trace. trail_mult 3.0 is NOT drift and NOT a birth defect: the block was introduced 2026-06-21 (#4069) with trail_mult 4.0, and 4.0 -> 3.0 was made 2026-07-12 in PR #6229, an operator-approved Tier-3 exit-lever package whose commit message names 'mes/mhg/tlt trail3' as one of 8 walk-forward cells ('Operator-approved 2026-07-12'). In that SAME commit mgc/xauusd went 3.0 -> 4.0, so trail3 for TLT was a per-leg choice, not a blanket. WHAT IS STALE IS THE COMMENT, not the field: the block still reads 'frac 0.5, trail 4.0' and cites the 2026-06-20 sweep, wrong for this field since 2026-07-12 (field beats comment). METHOD NOTE for whoever checks this next: the sandbox clone is SHALLOW by default, and on a shallow clone `git log -S` / `git log -L` over config/strategies.yaml return exactly ONE commit -- the graft boundary -- which reads as 'introduced here, never touched since' and is an ARTIFACT. It named a commit whose own message says 'Docs, matrix and backlog only -- no src/, no config/'. Run `git fetch --unshallow` first; the real count is 100 commits.

items.title: eth_pullback_2h fills 11 of 92 decisions (12.0%) — 81 signals never became a trade, and nothing measures why
items.detail:
SURFACED BY the M7 review packet generated 2026-08-16 (90d window, runtime_logs/strategy_reviews/2026-08-16/eth_pullback_2h.json): n_decisions 92, n_filled 11, n_closed 11 => fill_rate 12.0%.

This was invisible to every surface the review had been using. /api/bot/performance and /api/bot/strategy/attribution both aggregate CLOSED TRADES, so they describe the 11 that filled and say nothing about the 81 that did not. The packet is the only artifact that carries the decision denominator, which is exactly why the leg's 59-day-old review row could sit open while looking merely small.

WHY IT CHANGES THE READ ON THIS LEG: the operator's 2026-08-16 decision is to keep it live until n_closed reaches 20. At a 12% fill rate that requires roughly 75 MORE DECISIONS, not 9 more signals — which is the arithmetic behind the ~2.5-month estimate, and it is hostage to whatever is refusing 88% of them. If the refusals are a sizing or margin condition rather than genuine no-fills, the evidence clock may never run.

NOT YET DIAGNOSED — do not assume a cause. The candidates are distinguishable from data already written: (a) risk-refusals (RiskManager per-trade refusal rows carry a logged cause), (b) the netting guard's reentry_suppressed_netting_guard rows, (c) regime hard-gate drops (regime_hard_gate audit rows with enforced:true), (d) genuine non-fills of a limit/pending order. The packet itself reports all three regime cells at policy `unknown`, which makes (c) unlikely but does not exclude it.
items.resolution_criteria: The 81 unfilled decisions are ATTRIBUTED to causes with counts — a breakdown over order_packages.close_reason / the signals audit for strategy_name='eth_pullback_2h' across the same 90d window, summing to 81 with no residual bucket. Then either (i) the dominant cause is a legitimate market condition and the row closes as explained, or (ii) it is a refusal the operator can act on, and it gets its own Tier-2/3 item. The row must NOT be closed on a partial breakdown that leaves an unexplained remainder — an unstated denominator is what hid this in the first place.

updates.note: Filed rather than fixed: the diagnosis is one audit_query away but the operator's live decision this session was the disposition of the leg, not this. Flagged to them in-conversation as a NEW finding from the packet.

items.title: A p80 exit arm swept over a pooled multi-era population encodes a volatility mix the live book does not sample
items.summary:
MEASURED, not argued. risk/entry is exactly atr_stop_mult x ATR/close on both the live modules and both harnesses (identical formulas; byte-identical _atr), so cap_R = 0.099/(atr_stop_mult x ATR/close) -- i.e. a declared arm A on a leg with stop-mult M can only fire while ATR/close <= 0.099/(M*A). Reachability is therefore a function of the VOLATILITY REGIME at entry, not a property of the leg.

Relay #9710, config-exact, --tp-cap-pct 0.099, entry-conditioned: gld_pullback_1d arm 5.06 is reachable on 42/112 (37.5%) POOLED over 2010-2026 -- but 7/7 in 2018 and 1/7 across 2025-2026, against a live basis of 0/8. The pooled number describes no regime in particular. The effect is regime-CLUSTERED, not a trend: 2010-2013, 2020 and 2025-2026 are high-vol clusters separated by quiet 2014-2019 and 2022-2024.

This is what made the live-vs-backtest 'population splice' look irreconcilable. Held at fixed era the two populations AGREE (14.3% backtest vs 0% live, n=7 and n=8).
items.detail:
Root of the arm-above-cap class, and it is mechanical rather than per-leg bad luck. The six shipped p80 arms (BTC 6.49, xrp 4.49, avax 4.86, sol_4h 5.57, qqq 3.56, gld 5.06) were produced 2026-07-12/13 (S-M20-EXIT-REFINEMENT-2026-07-12.md:534). The harness first gained --tp-cap-pct on 2026-08-10 (BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP; m20_corpus_relabel_tp_cap.py dates the bracketing runs to 22:23Z/22:31Z that day). So all six are p80s of an UNCAPPED MFE distribution applied to a CAPPED live book, derived ~4 weeks before the harness could model the cap at all.

The theory predicts which legs break -- those whose uncapped p80 exceeds their own median ceiling -- and it holds 3/3 on the legs measured: gld 5.06 > 4.30 (37.5% reachable), qqq 3.56 > 2.70 (19.8%), scha 2.00 < 2.65 (83.1% reachable, and scha's 2.00 is NOT one of the six uncapped p80 arms).

NOT proposing any arm value here. Two remedies, either sufficient, both reporting-side.
items.suggested_action: (1) Have the sweep report each proposed arm's implied ATR/close ceiling (0.099/(atr_stop_mult*arm)) beside the arm, so a reader can check it against the current regime without re-deriving the identity; and/or (2) report the p80 PER ERA, or sweep on the recent era, so a pooled figure is never the only one quoted. Both are changes to m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py output, not to any config value.
items.resolution_criteria:
TWO REMEDIES, BOTH REQUIRED; the row stays open until both are done and each is verified on a REAL artefact rather than a merged writer.
(1) REACHABILITY REPORTING — DONE and verified 2026-08-16 (#9730 / relay #9734): verdicts.json carries p80_arm_reach with arm_reach_verdict, the measured TP-reach numbers, and the implied ATR/close ceiling; both verdict branches observed on two legs. Note its MEASURED limitation above: it grades against the backtest ceiling only.
(2) PER-ERA p80 — DONE and verified on a REAL artefact 2026-08-16 (#9789 `d8db5c59`; verdicts.json read in relay #9794). ORIGINAL TEXT, kept because the bar it set is the reason this closes: "NOT DONE. The sweep must report either a per-era p80 breakdown or an explicit recent-era p80, verified by reading a verdicts.json produced after that change on a leg whose pooled and recent-era figures DIFFER. Until a real run shows both figures with differing values, this half stays open: a writer that emits the key on a leg where the two coincide has demonstrated nothing."  — SATISFIED: both verification legs DIFFER, so the "a writer that emits the key on a leg where the two coincide has demonstrated nothing" clause is met rather than dodged. trend_donchian pooled 5.5R (n=95) vs recent-era 6.35R (n=17, span 2025), delta +0.85R. gld_pullback_1d — the discriminating leg session_01Xk2ozj named — pooled 3.86R (n=40) vs recent-era 4.96R (n=10, span 2017-2020), delta +1.10R.
items.first_half_shipped_and_verified_2026_08_: SHIPPED #9730 (7da0842) and VERIFIED against a real verdicts.json produced after the change (relay #9734, freshness-gated so a pre-change artefact could not be mistaken for this run's output). Both branches exercised on two legs, so one constant could not have satisfied both: trend_donchian_sol_4h p80 1.5R vs measured median TP reach 1.324R -> above_measured_median_ceiling (loud warning fired); gld_pullback_1d p80 3.86R vs 4.781R -> within_measured_median_ceiling. Printed ceilings reproduce the helper exactly (2.640% and 1.282%).
items.measured_limitation_the_verification_exp: ⚠️ THE SHIPPED CHECK CATCHES HALF THE CLASS, AND MISSES THE MOTIVATING CASE. It compares the proposed arm to the BACKTEST's measured ceiling. gld_pullback_1d's p80 3.86R is WITHIN its backtest median (4.781R) and so passes silently — while its LIVE cap_R is 2.20-3.01, i.e. 3.86R is unreachable on the book that trades (0 of 8 live entries). That is the population gap this whole row is about, so the check cannot close it by construction. An earlier description of the change called it 'the check that would have caught the whole arm-above-cap class' — that was an OVERCLAIM, discovered by verifying my own output rather than trusting the tests, and the code comment has been corrected. Closing the remaining half needs a LIVE-population input the sweep does not have; M31 P4 (backtest<->live MFE parity) is the piece that would supply it. A within_measured_median_ceiling verdict must NOT be read as 'reachable in production'.

second_half_shipped_and_verified_2026_08.the_dispersion_is_the_finding: trend_donchian's per-year p80 swings 3.87 -> 6.35 across five years, a 64% spread. That is this row's thesis measured on one leg: the pooled 5.5R describes no regime in particular, and nothing in the artifact said so before.
second_half_shipped_and_verified_2026_08.floor_is_measured_not_picked: _ERA_MIN_WINNERS = 10, set from per-year winner counts across all eight arm-declaring legs (relay #9788) and recorded in the constant's own comment. second_half_shipped_and_verified_2026_08.A_PREDICTION_I_GOT_WRONG_AND_WHY_IT_MATT: I predicted gld's recent-era span would be 2023-2025. It is 2017-2020, because resolve_split gives that leg a PER-LEG split of 2020-03-03 while my probe had used the default 2025-07-01 — so IS ends in 2020 and the newest year within IS is 2020, not 2025. The field is self-documenting and said so (era_basis: calendar_year_within_IS, span published), which is exactly why 'recent' was never labelled plain 'recent'. Had it been, this artifact would read as a claim about 2023-2025 that it does not make.

A year with no winners has NO row rather than a fabricated n=0. Every bucket ships its n.
second_half_shipped_and_verified_2026_08.changes_nothing_live: Reporting only. No arm value, verdict, or disposition moved; the era figures are never fed to --trail-decay-arm-r (pinned by test_era_block_never_feeds_the_arm).

the_mechanism_is_now_measured_not_inferr.claim: This row states the six shipped arms are p80s of an UNCAPPED book, inferred from dates (swept 2026-07-12/13; the harness gained --tp-cap-pct 2026-08-10). That is now MEASURED.

The naive comparison (today's capped p80 vs the shipped arm) was NOT used: it conflates cap, split, data vintage and code drift.
the_mechanism_is_now_measured_not_inferr.reading: Four of seven legs reproduce the shipped arm from the UNCAPPED book within 0.35R and xrp_pullback_2h is exact. The arms were not chosen against the book that trades.
the_mechanism_is_now_measured_not_inferr.CAVEAT_THE_TWO_ARMS_ARE_DIFFERENT_POPULA: Winner counts differ between arms (sol_4h 69 capped vs 41 uncapped; xrp 90 vs 67) because the cap acts as a take-profit and banks winners that would otherwise round-trip. items.tier: 3 (moves where order geometry is resolved, and would change the TP actually placed on live legs)
items.title: _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT is a Bybit ErrCode 10001 workaround applied unconditionally; on the ALPACA-ONLY legs (GLD, SCHA) no venue is known to require it
items.summary:
_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT = 0.099 is documented at trend_donchian.py:125-132 as a Bybit workaround ('Bybit (and most exchanges) reject TP further than ~10% from the reference base price, ErrCode 10001'). It is a module-level constant with NO venue branch, used directly in the tp formula in four strategy modules.

Three legs that declare a trail_decay_arm_r are carried by NO Bybit account (config/accounts.yaml): gld_pullback_1d (GLD -> alpaca_paper/alpaca_portfolio/alpaca_live), qqq_trend_long_1d (QQQ -> ib_paper + the three Alpaca accounts), scha_trend_long_1d (SCHA -> alpaca_paper). The value is not re-derived downstream either: pkg.tp reaches Alpaca verbatim as take_profit.limit_price (alpaca_client.py:189), and that client carries no distance check.

Consequence on those legs: the cap sets a real profit exit at cap_R (gld ~4.3R at median vol, ~1.3R in 2026) rather than acting as the never-filling 50R sentinel it is documented to be -- and it is what makes their declared arms unreachable.
items.detail:
NOT ESTABLISHED, and must not be assumed: that Alpaca or IBKR would ACCEPT a farther take-profit. That was not tested and cannot be without placing an order; absence of a distance check in our client is not proof the venue lacks one. Establishing it is the first step, and it is cheap on a paper account.

The unconditional application also has a real structural reason rather than being simple oversight: tp is computed in the signal builder, which runs BEFORE per-account routing, so no account or venue is in scope at that point. Per-leg the venue set IS knowable from config (a leg's symbols determine which accounts are eligible), so a per-leg resolution is possible -- but it moves where order geometry is decided, which is why this is Tier-3 and not a one-line fix.

Interacts with PB-20260816-ARM-SWEEP-POOLS-VOL-ERAS: if the cap should not bind on these legs, then --tp-cap-pct 0.099 is the correct LIVE-PARITY setting for the harness today (it faithfully reproduces what the code does) while being the wrong setting for what the code SHOULD do. Do not 'fix' the harness default in response to this row.

SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-16 (see scope_correction_2026_08_16): a package fanning out to BOTH Alpaca and IBKR must satisfy the TIGHTER rule, so a venue-aware cap would have to resolve per ROUTE, not per leg. That is materially harder than 'look up the leg's venue' and raises the cost of the Tier-3 change.
items.suggested_action: Step 1 (Tier-1, cheap): establish empirically whether Alpaca and IBKR accept a bracket take-profit further than 10% from entry, on a paper account. If they do, Step 2 (Tier-3): propose resolving the cap per leg from the venues its symbols route to, with the exact diff, and re-sweep the affected arms against the corrected ceiling.
items.resolution_criteria: POPULATION: the 2 ALPACA-ONLY arm-declaring legs — gld_pullback_1d (GLD, n=112) and scha_trend_long_1d (SCHA, n=65), measured entry-conditioned 2010-03-26 to 2026-06-12 (relay #9710). qqq_trend_long_1d is excluded: it also routes to ib_paper, where a ~10% NBBO rule may make the cap correct. Closes on EITHER (a) a recorded paper-account result showing Alpaca REFUSES a take-profit further than 9.9% of entry, which closes this as correct-as-is with the evidence attached; or (b) Alpaca accepts it AND the cap resolution is made route-aware with operator approval, verified by reading a live order package on an Alpaca-routed leg whose tp is no longer clamped to entry*1.099. A code change alone does NOT close it — the check is a real order package with an un-clamped tp, because the clamp lives in a signal builder that runs before per-account routing, so a fix applied at the wrong layer would look correct in diff and change nothing. Reading more documentation does NOT close it either: the open question is an undocumented API validation, which only an order attempt reveals.
items.scope_correction_2026_08_16: NARROWED after checking the venues' own rules — the row's ID still says 'AND-IB-LEGS' and is kept as a stable handle, but the IB half does NOT hold. Alpaca's public docs document NO maximum take-profit distance (only a $0.01 minimum stop offset and take_profit.limit_price better than stop_loss.stop_price) — read 2026-08-16. IBKR is REPORTED to reject stock orders priced more than ~10% from NBBO (20% options), which would make the 9.9% cap approximately CORRECT on that route; that figure is a search summary and NOT verified — both IBKR primary pages returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher. So the finding holds for the Alpaca-only legs gld_pullback_1d and scha_trend_long_1d, and qqq_trend_long_1d is NOT a clean instance because it also routes to ib_paper. The code comment's parenthetical 'Bybit (AND MOST EXCHANGES)' was more accurate than the original reading of it.

items.tier: 1 (a docstring/consumer question; the clamp itself is correct and no runtime behaviour is proposed)
items.title: exit_plan_state.targets[].reach_r is an OBSERVE-ONLY clamped counterfactual; reading it as the reachability ceiling manufactures false `inert` on any arm above 5.0R
items.summary:
SETTLED BY READING THE PLACEMENT PATH, after this row was filed with its direction inverted AND then 'corrected' in the wrong direction. The operative ceiling is the VENUE TP cap, 0.099/(risk_per_unit/entry) -- the value `order_packages.tp` encodes and the broker is sent: `execute.py:391` builds `"tp": pkg.tp`; `:703`/`:1467` send `kwargs["takeProfit"] = quantize_price(order["tp"], tick)`; `:1875`/`:1912` journal `take_profit_1 = float(pkg.tp)`.

`exit_plan_state.targets[].reach_r` is `min(venue_cap_R, DEFAULT_MAX_REACH_R=5.0)` from the ExitPlan ladder, which is OBSERVE-ONLY and never placed: the sole exit-plan reference in `execute.py` is the soak block at `:630-648` ("nothing reads it back"), and `exit_plan_state` appears nowhere else in `src/` except the materializer and DB serialization. So reading it UNDER-reports and manufactures false `inert`.

BLAST RADIUS: it caps every observation at 5.0, so the three arms ABOVE the clamp -- trend_donchian 6.49, trend_donchian_sol_4h 5.57, gld_pullback_1d 5.06 -- would grade a blanket false `inert` (trend_donchian flips from reachable-at-100% to inert). Arms BELOW 5.0 are provably unaffected: min(x,5) >= arm iff x >= arm when arm < 5, which is why xrp_pullback_2h's 2/37 (arm 4.49) is correct as recorded.

NO LANDED VERDICT IS WRONG, checked individually rather than assumed: trend_donchian's p50 11.91 came from `scripts/ops/lever_reachability_audit.py`, which computes `cap_pct / risk_over_entry` (the venue cap) directly; gld's live rows were 2.20-3.01, all below the clamp; uso is basis-independent at arm 1.0; xrp is preserved by the inequality above. What WAS wrong is guidance, now corrected in this file's basis_note.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN: `src/runtime/position_telemetry.py::cap_r` computes the venue cap and is therefore CORRECT for reachability -- the earlier claim in this row that it needed a min() against the clamp was a consequence of the inverted reading and is withdrawn. The residual is a DOCSTRING question: `lever_reachability_audit.py::cap_r` says 'the highest MFE in R a trade can print before its capped TP fills', which is right, while the observe-only ladder carries a field that looks like the same quantity and is not. Nothing enforces that a future reader picks the right one.
items.resolution_criteria: Add a docstring note at `src/runtime/exit_plan_realism.py::clamp_exit_plan` (and/or the `exit_plan_state` column comment in `src/units/db/database.py`) stating that the clamped target is OBSERVE-ONLY and must not be read as the reachability ceiling, naming the venue cap as the operative one. Verifiable by grepping `DEFAULT_MAX_REACH_R` and confirming the observe-only status is stated where the value is produced, not only in the registry's basis_note (which a code-side reader never opens). Closing on 'the registry documents it' is NOT sufficient -- that is the surface that already had it and still produced two inverted revisions in one session.
