items.tier: 1 (measurement + a reporting script; the arm VALUES it would inform stay Tier-3)
items.title: M31 P4 (backtest<->live MFE parity) preconditions: the quantities ARE comparable, the soak population is EMPTY (0 closed rows), and finality is only knowable via a join nothing enforces
items.summary:
MEASURED 2026-08-16, not argued. P4 is gated in the design on 'P2 soak depth'. Three preconditions were checked before treating depth as the only gate; two pass and one is a real constraint on how P4 must be written.

(a) COMPARABLE — live `trail_decay.since_entry_peak` computes (max(window.high) - entry)/risk and the harness `_ratchet` computes max(mfe, (ext - entry)/risk) over bar highs. Same numerator, same denominator, same bar-extreme basis. P4 is well-posed.

(b) EMPTY, not shallow — /api/bot/db/table/position_telemetry returns total: 12, filter_state: not_requested, and ALL TWELVE are open positions. There are ZERO closed-trade rows, so P4 has no terminal MFE to compare against. Expected (P2 shipped the same day) but 'needs more depth' and 'has nothing in it' are different statements.

(c) FINALITY NEEDS A JOIN — the table has NO status/closed_at/is_final column, so a row cannot say whether its peak_r is final or still accruing, and an open trade's peak_r is a LOWER BOUND. trade_id is populated 12/12 so position_telemetry.trade_id -> trades.status works, but nothing enforces it.
items.detail:
WHY (c) IS THE ONE THAT BITES. A parity check that pools open and closed trades would systematically understate the live side -- not by a modelling error but by averaging unfinished trades against finished ones. It would look like a real backtest-optimism finding and be an artifact of the population. This is the unstated-population class the repo already has a top-level rule for.

A HAZARD CHECKED AND REFUTED, so nobody re-derives it: the fleet sweep warns that a bar spanning from below the stop to far above the target 'books a -1R loss AND records a huge MFE' (ict_scalp_avax_5m, 182.34R over four trades). If the harness ratcheted MFE on the stopping bar, backtest MFE would exceed anything live could observe by convention alone. It does NOT for this family: backtest_pullback evaluates _stop_or_target BEFORE _ratchet and breaks on a hit (:592-601), and arm C does the same per sub-bar (:579-585). The 182.34R case is the ict_scalp harness, a DIFFERENT one -- so the hazard is real but scoped, and the donchian/pullback family (where every telemetry row with a declared arm lives) is clean.

THE RESIDUAL ASYMMETRY RUNS THE OTHER WAY and is unquantified: the backtest excludes the exit bar entirely, while live peak_r includes however much of the terminal bar had formed at the last monitor pass. Bounded and small, but it biases live HIGH, which is the opposite of the naive expectation -- so a small positive live-minus-backtest gap is NOT automatically evidence of backtest optimism.

COLLATERAL CORROBORATION (recorded because it came from a different data path than the registry): both telemetry rows carrying a declared trail_decay_arm_r show the arm ABOVE the live cap_r -- xrp_pullback_2h arm 4.49 vs cap_r 3.9233 on bybit_2 (REAL MONEY), qqq_trend_long_1d arm 3.56 vs cap_r 2.1258 on alpaca_paper. Both agree with config/lever_reachability.json's verdicts (vol_conditional / inert), which were derived from order_packages/risk_per_unit rather than from this table.
items.suggested_action: When the soak has closed rows: (1) write the parity script to JOIN trades.status and restrict to finished trades, reporting the closed-row count as its denominator the way rCoverage/pnlCoverage do; (2) report per-leg, since the harness convention differs by FAMILY (pullback/donchian stop-first vs ict_scalp) and a fleet aggregate would mix two conventions; (3) quantify the terminal-bar asymmetry once rather than assuming it away. Consider whether P2 should stamp a terminal snapshot flag so finality stops depending on a join no consumer is obliged to make -- that is a P2 change, not a P4 one.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when a parity run exists that (a) states its closed-trade denominator, (b) is restricted to finished trades via trades.status, and (c) reports per-leg or per-family rather than one fleet number. A run that reports a single pooled figure over a population including open trades does NOT close this row -- that is the artifact this row exists to prevent.

items.tier: 1 to WIRE (a read path over two committed artefacts). Every arm_r verdict it would inform stays Tier-3 and the operator's.
items.title: config/lever_reachability.json has been buying entry-conditioned cap_R one leg at a time via bespoke relays, while m20-sweep-corpus already carries the same measurement for 34 legs and nothing reads it
items.source: Found while tracing why tonight's 52 corpus rows lacked live_tp_reach_r_* (BL-20260816-CORPUS-CONFLICT-REDERIVE-RUNS-THE-STALE-BRANCH-EXTRACTOR). Chasing the dropped field surfaced that where it DOES survive, it has no consumer.
items.why_it_matters: This is the written-and-never-read shape provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch, and it has a measurable cost rather than being merely untidy: the registry's own basis_note discredits the cheap candle screen ('NOT a bound in either direction — on xrp it overstated reachability 90.5% vs 33.3% because entries are filter-selected') and therefore needs an ENTRY-CONDITIONED population. It has been obtaining exactly that with a bespoke relay run per leg — #9710 for scha_trend_long_1d, #9715 for trend_donchian_sol_4h — while every fleet sweep since #9037 has been writing the same class of number into the corpus for free. Two of the eight registry rows still read `unmeasured`/`queued_tier3`.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: for a leg whose registry row carries NO entry-conditioned basis, the corpus alone yields cap_R median/min/max/n and a reach share against that leg's arm_r, without dispatching a relay. Demonstrate on a leg that currently has none — reproducing a leg that already has a bespoke block proves only that the join works where the answer was already known.
items.next_action: Join docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl's live_tp_reach_r_{n,median,min,max}_{IS,OOS} onto config/lever_reachability.json by leg, as a RECORDED SECONDARY basis with the caveat below — never as a verdict flip. The natural home is scripts/ci/check_lever_reachability.py (which today has ZERO references to the field) or the coverage roll-up. Cheapest first step is a read-only report, not a writer.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-16 against merged main.

COVERAGE. 376 of 1264 corpus rows carry a non-null live_tp_reach_r_n_IS, spanning 34 legs. The registry holds 8 lever rows; 7 of those 8 legs have a corpus measurement (qqq_trend_long_1d is the one with none).

NO CONSUMER. live_tp_reach_r / tp_r_effective appears in the four backtest harnesses (which compute it), m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py (which surfaces it), m20_corpus_extract.py (which writes it), three test files and two sprint logs. scripts/ci/check_lever_reachability.py: 0 references. config/lever_reachability.json: 0 references. Nothing decides anything with it.

IT AGREES WITH THE BESPOKE RELAYS WHERE BOTH EXIST — the check that makes the join trustworthy rather than merely available:
  * trend_donchian_sol_4h (arm 5.57): bespoke cap_r_at_median 1.64 over n=127 (relay #9715, span 2023-01-09→2026-06-29, reach 0/127 = 0.0%) vs corpus median 1.324 over n=135. The corpus MAX is 3.723 — strictly below the 5.57 arm — so the corpus independently gives 0/135 reachable, reproducing the bespoke zero without the relay.
  * scha_trend_long_1d (arm 2.00): bespoke cap_r_at_median 2.65 over n=65 (relay #9710, span 2010-03-10→2026-06-12, reach 54/65 = 83.1%) vs corpus medians 2.81/3.058/3.122 over n=60. Arm 2.00 sits below every one, agreeing with 'largely reachable'.
The residual gap in the medians is explained by population, not method: the corpus figure is the sweep's IS window at a DERIVED split, the bespoke figure is the leg's complete backtest span.

⚠️ THE CAVEAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE NUMBER, OR THE JOIN MANUFACTURES FALSE `reachable` VERDICTS. The harnesses place tp = min(entry*1.099, entry + tp_r*risk) and every leg declares the sentinel tp_r = 50.0, so tp_r_effective IS the venue-cap identity 0.099/(risk/entry) — which is quantity (3) in the registry's own basis_note taxonomy, NOT the operative ceiling (1) exit_plan_state.targets[].reach_r. src/runtime/exit_plan_realism.py's DEFAULT_MAX_REACH_R = 5.0 clamps first wherever cap_R > 5.0, so a corpus median above 5.0 OVER-reports the reach a lever actually gets. That bites today: trend_donchian's corpus median is 5.833 and its max 36.439, both past the clamp. So the corpus basis is strictly better than the discredited candle screen (entry-conditioned, large-n) and strictly weaker than the live order_packages/risk_per_unit basis — the same standing the registry already assigns its own backtest_entry_conditioned_* blocks, whose basis_caveat wording should be reused verbatim rather than reinvented.

CHANGES NOTHING TODAY. No verdict, disposition or arm_r moves here. The three queued_tier3 rows (xrp_pullback_2h, trend_donchian_sol_4h, scha_trend_long_1d) remain the operator's call; this records that the evidence for two of them was already sitting in a committed artefact.

items.title: position_telemetry has no terminal snapshot and no finality marker — M31 P4's blocking half
items.source: docs/sprint-logs/S-M31-P4-MFE-PARITY-2026-08-17.md
items.detail: docs/design/position-telemetry-DESIGN.md section 7.2 recommends 'live row + a terminal snapshot written at close', explicitly so P4 gets 'one honest per-trade MFE without per-bar volume'. The live row shipped in P2; the terminal snapshot did not. Verified by reading src/runtime/position_telemetry.py (write_record is an UPSERT on order_package_id, no close path) and its only two callers, src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:967 and htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:534, both on the OPEN-position monitor path. Two consequences: (a) a closed trade's peak_r is the value at the LAST EXIT PASS BEFORE the close, so every live MFE is a lower bound of unquantified size; (b) the table carries no status/closed_at/terminal marker, so a closed row is byte-shaped like an open one and finality is only obtainable via a trade_id -> trades.status join. Measured 2026-08-17: 14 telemetry rows, 13 open and 1 closed (trade 4697, trend_donchian_sol_4h), where the closed row's only in-table hint was a staler updated_at — which is not a signal, since a quiet leg and a closed leg both go stale.
items.why_it_matters: This is the collapsed-state class the repo has a canonical rule and a CI guard for (docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md section 'Collapsed states'), in a table shipped after that rule: 'we did not look' and 'we looked and it is final' are indistinguishable. It is also the concrete blocker on M31 P4 Check B, which is the named binding blocker for the arm-reachability programme — the fleet sweep grades p80_arm_reach only against the BACKTEST ceiling, and gld_pullback_1d passes that at 3.86R while being unreachable live (0 of 8).
items.resolution_criteria: A terminal write at close (Tier-2, on the close path) that stamps finality explicitly, so a consumer can distinguish final from in-flight WITHOUT the trades join; and the lower bound either closed or quantified. Registering the finality field with collapsed-state-guard is what makes it enforced rather than merely present.
items.next_action: Propose the terminal-snapshot writer as a Tier-2 change (operator OK needed — it touches the live close path). Until then scripts/research/m31_mfe_parity.py refuses to grade without --trades-json, so nothing silently reads an open row as final.

updates.note: RESOLVED (Tier-2, operator-approved in-conversation). Database.update_trade now stamps position_telemetry.terminal_state='final' + terminal_at when a row transitions to closed, in its own guard mirroring _record_trade_cost_estimate so a telemetry write failure can neither propagate into nor be skipped by the trader close path. Never overwrites an existing stamp (a re-close must not move terminal_at forward -- first observation is the honest one, the netting reconciler's anchor rule) and never INSERTS a row (manufacturing one at close would fabricate a trajectory that was never measured). Readers publish a four-state finality_source -- stamped / derived_join / not_final / unknown -- so a row that predates the writer can never read as one the close hook stamped; registered with collapsed-state-guard as position_telemetry.finality_source per this item's own resolution criteria, and mutation-tested (collapsing derived_join into stamped makes the guard fire). Idempotent migration for pre-existing DBs, placed AFTER the telemetry DDL -- an empty PRAGMA table_info means no such table, so the original placement in the trades migration block raised on every fresh DB.

items.residual: The peak_r LOWER BOUND is NARROWED, not eliminated. The stamp marks the row final at the close observation, but peak_r is still the value from the last exit pass BEFORE the close, and a bar extreme cannot see an intrabar excursion. So peak_r_is_lower_bound stays true on every row, including stamped ones. Quantifying that residual gap is separate work and is why M31 P5 does not propose a peak_r-driven giveback lever first.

items.title: The sprint-log format is documented as MANDATORY and nothing enforces it
items.source: docs/sprint-logs/S-M31-HARNESS-MFE-DIST-2026-08-17.md
items.detail: CLAUDE.md's instruction hierarchy names docs/SPRINT-LOG-TEMPLATE-CANONICAL.md as the 'mandatory sprint-log format' (14 '## ' sections). NOTHING checks it. Probe: grep -rl 'SPRINT-LOG-TEMPLATE-CANONICAL' over scripts/, tests/ and .github/ returns ZERO files. The probe is not blind -- the template itself is findable at docs/SPRINT-LOG-TEMPLATE-CANONICAL.md, and the same grep finds the canonical-doc-coherence and artifact-validity guards for the docs they DO cover, so a zero here is absence rather than a broken search. MEASURED DRIFT on logs written 2026-08-17: S-M20-WF-EFFECTIVE-FOLDS 15 sections, S-M31-TERMINAL-STAMP 10, S-M31-P4-MFE-PARITY 10, and the first version of S-M31-HARNESS-MFE-DIST (mine) 7. Note 15 > 14 is not itself a defect (extra sections are fine); the finding is the SHORTFALLS, and the count alone cannot distinguish the two -- a guard must check section NAMES, not a total.
items.why_it_matters: The sections that go missing are the ones a later session reads to decide whether to trust the log: 'Repo State Checked', 'Contradictions or Drift Found', 'Deferred Items', 'Wrap-Up Check'. A log missing 'Deferred Items' reads as a completed unit of work when it may have deferred the load-bearing half -- which is exactly the shape of this session's own work, where the mechanism shipped and the artifact did not. This is the same family as BL-20260817-COLLAPSED-STATE-SELFTEST-REGISTERED-BUT-NEVER-INVOKED: a control that is declared and never executed. Here the 'control' is a documented mandatory format.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a CI check that every file added under docs/sprint-logs/ carries all 14 '## ' section names from the template -- diff-scoped so the ~200 existing logs are grandfathered, the same shape as diagnostic-provenance-guard -- with a self-test proving it FAILS on a log missing a section (not merely passes on a good one); or (b) an explicit decision, recorded in CLAUDE.md, that the template is advisory rather than mandatory, so the hierarchy stops claiming an enforcement that does not exist. Either resolves it; the current state -- 'mandatory' with zero enforcement and measured drift -- is the one that should not persist.
items.next_action: A review session picks (a) or (b). If (a): grandfather by diff scope, and check NAMES not a count. Cheap either way; the measurement above is the whole investigation.

items.title: expectancyR and dollar PnL disagree in SIGN on multiple legs — trend_donchian_ada_4h reports 62.6R expectancy, ict_scalp_5m reports +34.84R on real money against -$0.54
items.detail:
POPULATION: closed non-backtest trades in the /api/bot/performance 30d window (since 2026-07-22, read 2026-08-21). Measured per-strategy:
  paper trend_donchian_ada_4h  n=7 trades   totalPnl +2006.65   expectancyR 62.615   totalR 438.30
  REAL  ict_scalp_5m           n=6 trades   totalPnl    -0.54   expectancyR  5.806   totalR  34.84
  REAL  headline 30d           n=24 trades  totalPnl    +1.70   expectancyR  1.2525  totalR  30.06   rCoverage 1.0
The real-money 30d book therefore reads +30.06R on +$1.70, and 34.84 of those 30.06 R come from ONE leg whose dollars are negative. Over the same 24 trades rCoverage is 1.0, so this is not a thin-sample artifact of the R denominator being absent — it is present and wrong.

An expectancy of 62.615 R per trade over 7 trades is not a trading result; it is an R denominator (|entry - stop| x qty) collapsing toward zero on a leg whose stop sat very close to entry, e.g. after a trail. Because totalR SUMS across legs, one such leg poisons every aggregate above it.

CLAUDE.md's 'Dollars are the scoreboard' rule and the R4 research->results gate both depend on R being comparable across instruments. On this population it is not. | ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-22 (Phase-2 item 2.4). MEASURED, /api/bot/performance?window=30d, real-money, n=29 closed, rCoverage=1.0 (so this is NOT a coverage gap -- the endpoint believes every trade's risk is known). 3 of 6 per-strategy rows disagree in sign: ict_scalp_5m pnl -$0.03 vs totalR +38.445; trend_donchian pnl +$12.82 vs totalR -3.032 (4 trades, ZERO shorts); xrp_pullback_2h pnl +$5.29 vs totalR -0.190. | TWO HYPOTHESES REFUTED, not merely unselected. (a) A short/long sign error: the disagreeing strategies are 37.5% short vs 57.1% for the agreeing ones -- the correlation runs the WRONG WAY -- and trend_donchian has no shorts at all. (b) A sign error in the denominator: _clean_trades.r_multiple uses abs(entry-stop), so a per-trade R can never disagree in sign with its own pnl. | THE ACTUAL MECHANISM IS WEIGHTING, NOT SIGN. totalR is a sum of pnl_i/risk_i while totalPnl is a sum of pnl_i, so a loser with a SMALL risk denominator outweighs several winners with large ones and flips the aggregate. The denominators go small because `trades.stop_loss` is the CURRENT stop, mutated by trailing-stop updates, not the INITIAL risk at entry: once a trailing stop ratchets toward the entry price, |entry-stop| -> 0 and R explodes. r_multiple's `risk <= 0` guard catches only EXACTLY zero, never NEAR zero. Measured instance: trade 4258 (ict_scalp_5m) carries risk of $0.372 on a $5.08 pnl => R = 13.6 from one row. Trade 4824 (trend_donchian) is a LONG whose stored stop 74479.1 sits ABOVE its entry 70888.9 -- not corruption, a trailing stop that ratcheted up on a winner, which is precisely why the value cannot serve as initial risk. | CONSEQUENCE: expectancyR is not an expectancy. It gates R-based promotion decisions while measuring a quantity that is not R, and rCoverage=1.0 reports full confidence in it. The fix is to normalise by the risk DECLARED AT ENTRY rather than by a column the exit path mutates -- so the fix is a data-availability question first (is entry-time risk stored anywhere today?), not a formula change. Deliberately NOT written here: changing what a promotion gate reads is Tier-3.
items.why_it_matters: R is the axis the promotion gates read. A leg whose R is computed against a near-zero denominator will clear any R-based gate while losing money, which is precisely the failure the gate exists to prevent. Measured here on 2 of 31 strategy rows across the real and paper 30d blocks, but the contamination is at the AGGREGATE level, so it reaches every consumer of totalR/expectancyR regardless of how few legs cause it.
items.next_action: Tier-1: floor or reject the R denominator when |entry - stop| is below a venue-tick-derived minimum, and report rTradeCount alongside a max|R| so a single outlier is visible. Then re-check whether any past promotion decision rested on an R aggregate containing one.
items.resolution_criteria: Over a 30d window of at least 20 closed trades, no per-strategy expectancyR exceeds a stated plausible bound without an explicit outlier annotation, and the real-money totalR sign matches its totalPnl sign.
